cues.text: Each point on this line is the price of Bitcoin at the end of one hour: the close.
Joined together, the hourly closes show where price has been.
We can plot the positions every time we create a new high. We label these positions as Higher Highs (HH).
We also plot the positions where we make a new low between each HH. We label these positions as Higher Lows (HL).
When we plot between the HH and HL positions we see a less noisy sawtooth gradually increasing on a lower-resolution plot.
Sometimes we get a dip where the low is not increasing. This cannot be called a Higher Low. These are called Lower Lows (LL).
We can see from the sawtooth that we are trending upwards.
Even though it may dip, it keeps returning to the previous high and beyond. We can note the position where this happens.
Where this happens we call it a Break of Structure (BoS).
This may coincide with an HH
Or not.
A swing is a range of positions. It begins at the position the BoS breaks and ends at the position of the BoS itself.
An Upswing is a swing that trends upwards.
The Swing Low is the lowest position in the swing. It is either an HL or an LL.
An Upswing is characterised by a downleg from the HH to the Swing Low, followed by an upleg from the Swing Low to the BoS.
Let's observe the upswings in real time.
Similarly we can plot the sawtooth in a downward trend where the highs are not Higher Highs, but Lower Highs (LH).
Even though it may peak, it keeps returning to the previous low and heads lower. We can note the position where this happens.
Where this happens we also call it a Break of Structure (BoS).
And we can define a Downswing, characterised by an upleg from the LL to the Swing High, followed by a downleg from the Swing High to the BoS.
We might notice the price heading back up.
If it breaks the previous HH

then it turns out the Downswings were just part of a longer term Upswing.
Our real time analysis might have considered this a Downswing, and we may have strategised according to this observation.
Where we may have considered something to have been observed, that later disappears with new data, we call it a Ghost, and in this case Ghost Downswings.
But the data Ghosts hide can be useful. Zooming in we can see the sawtooth pattern at a lower level.

Where this breaks the prior HL, we can note the position where this happens.
Where this happens we call it a Market Structure Break (MSB). Sometimes it is called a Change of Character.
Like the BoS, it may coincide with a turning point on the Sawtooth.
Or not.
At this point we don't know if it will continue down or complete an Upswing.
A swing does not need to be completed to observe a MSB.
Here, it happens we see the price bottom out and complete an Upswing.
A MSB can happen on an upward leg of a Sawtooth, where the price closes higher than the prior LH.
